tossups.text: The Peshmerga are the official military force of an autonomous region in the north of this country that includes the cities of Erbil and Halabja. Basra is this country's major port, despite being seventy miles upstream from the mouth of the Shatt-al-Arab. In the twentieth century, this country fought wars with its eastern and southeastern neighbors, Iran and Kuwait. For 10 points, name this Middle Eastern country whose capital is Baghdad.

In the opening battle of this war, artillery at Turtukai were used to push forces under PA Dannenburg from Oltenitza. Another battle began after Michael Gorchakov sent his generals a note reading, "Let's start it." That battle at the Chernaya was part of a larger siege during this war that included assaults on Alma, Inkerman and a fort called the Great Redan. Marechal Canrobert allied with Lord Raglan at another battle during this war which included an action called the "Thin Red Line." The battles of Balaclava and Sevastopol took place during, for 10 points, what war between Russia and a French-British-Ottoman alliance?

His early compositions such as Die Liebe für den König oder Karl Stuart and Nicht mehr als sechs Schüsseln were written while at the abbey of Kremsmunster under the direction of Georg Pasterwitz. Although he attained a degree of success after the opera Moses oder der Auszug aus Agypten, the theatre director needed convincing to stage his final opera, "List und Zufall." Paganini's reputation as a virtuoso was established when he wrote and performed a set of variations "on the G string" based on a theme in this composer's opera Il Noce de Benevento. Erich Duda catalogued this composer's work, including two German Requiems and the opera Der Spiegel von Arkadien, with a libretto written by Schikaneder. For 10 points identify this composer who completed a horn concerto and Requiem by Mozart.

AC Graham argued that leaders subscribing to this school of thought 'have no functions which could not be performed by an elementary computer', leading to the 'entrapped sovereign' paradox. A thinker from this school wrote that 'the people follow after benefit as water flows downward'. Another thinker from this school argued that texts written in 'bamboo strips' should be eliminated and that the only reason 'a minister does not murder his ruler' is due to insufficient preparations. That was one of the reasons this school argued for punitive laws known as fa. This school was advocated for by Shang Yang and Han Fei. For 10 points, name this Chinese school of philosophy that emphasises the importance of order through the use of harsh laws.

Description Acceptable. The beginning of a work made up of these texts recounts the protagonist getting beat up for supposedly "winking" at a boy at church. One of these texts mentions Miss Millie calling a character's actions "ungrateful" and is present alongside another of these texts which describes the Olinka tribe. One of these "chapters" describes a reunion at a July barbeque, while another describes a quilt being torn apart. A depiction of Corrine falling ill is present in one of these texts, another of which describes the protagonist's pursuit of a woman towards Memphis, Tennessee. Many of these texts describe a character's rape and abuse by Alphonso, while some describe their writer's affair with the blues singer Shug Avery. For 10 points, name these epistles that make up an Alice Walker novel.
acceptableAnswers: anything of that nature in The Color Purple until “chapters” is read

tossups.text: This city's Opzoomer Street names a type of community-organized urban renewal movement. The Lijnbaan shopping street in this city was the first planned pedestrian street in Europe. Ossip Zadkine's sculpture The Destroyed City commemorates this city's World War II bombing. Dubbed "The Swan" for its asymmetrical pylon, this city's Erasmus Bridge crosses the New Meuse River. This is the largest city protected by the Delta Works. Due to its Europoort, this city in the Rhine-Meuse-Scheldt Delta is the largest seaport in Europe. For 10 points, name this city that forms a metropolitan area with The Hague and is the second largest city in the Netherlands.

This author created the University College of Abertawe professor Athro Haines, who wrote a book on "medieval Cwmrhydyceirw" that the protagonist pretends to have heard of to impress his boss. Philip Larkin and this author created a game where they would replace words in literary quotes with obscenities, like "I have gathered up six slender basketfuls OF HORSEPISS." The "shadowy Argentinian outfit" for which this author wrote a Graham Greene monograph inspired his character of Dr. L. S. Caton, who plagiarizes an article on medieval shipbuilding. The ghost of Dr. Underhill conjures a being made of twigs to haunt the title inn of a novel by this author. This author of The Green Man wrote a novel in which a lecture on "Merrie England' is drunkenly delivered by Professor Dixon. For 10 points, name this author of Lucky Jim.

A poem with this title speculates "maybe the Almighty Himself has turned a bit bourgeois / and uses a credit card" after stating that "the last twenty years were good for practically everybody, / save the dead." Gertrude Stein's The Making of Americans was published in an influential modernist review whose name, which was stylized in lowercase, included this adjective; in addition to editing The English Review, Ford Madox Ford ran that magazine in 1924. This adjective titles a 2013 novel in which Frederick Douglass's visit to Ireland inspires the housemaid Lily to move to America, written by Colum McCann. A misspelling of this adjective titles a novel in which Puto obsesses over young boys such as Ignacy; that novel is based on the escape of its author, Witold Gombrowicz, from Poland to Argentina. For 10 points, identify this compound adjective that names the slave trade that brought Phillis Wheatley to America, as well as a branch of studies that examines literary linkages across a certain ocean.

A national park in this state is named for the author of The Yearling, Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings. Part of this state's northern border is along the St. Mary's River. Another national park in this state contains the Western Hemisphere's largest masonry structure, Fort Jefferson. Since 1565, this state's European settlement of Saint Augustine has been continuously occupied. This state, home to Dry Tortugas National Park, is also home to an 885-square-mile city on its eastern coast and to a freshwater lake, Okeechobee. For 10 points, name this state home to Jacksonville, the Everglades, and Walt Disney World.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for reflex arcs. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this spinal cord-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The spinal cord is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in reflex arcs.

tossups.text: The innermost of these entities are assumed to be completely filled in the frozen core approximation. The changes in their energies due to changes in geometry are depicted in Walsh diagrams. In certain cases, their energies can be approximated in terms of exchange, Coulomb, and overlap integrals. The conservation of their symmetry is the basis of the Woodward-Hoffman rules. According to Fukui, who developed their namesake "frontier" theory, chemical reactivity only depends on the highest occupied and lowest unoccupied examples of them. They always come in pairs, with the higher-energy one marked with a star and designated as "antibonding." For 10 points, name these functions that can be calculated as linear combinations of atomic orbitals.

The first scene of this play's third act ends with a giant mirror descending and covering two characters as the final movement of Mozart's "Dissonance" quartet plays. Before that mirror descends, one of those characters orders the other to confess at gunpoint after hearing him correct the name of a brutal soldier from "Bud" to "Stud." This play opens with its main female character crouching down to hide from the headlights of an approaching car. A flat tire causes a doctor to give a ride home to a member of an investigative commission corresponding to the real-life Rettig Commission. Upon seeing that doctor, this play's only female character ties him up and orders him to confess to raping and torturing her. Throughout this play, Gerardo Escobar and his wife Paulina Salas struggle over how to treat Dr. Roberto Miranda, a former torturer in a dictatorship based on the regime of Augusto Pinochet. Named for the piece of music played by Dr. Miranda before torturing victims, For 10 points, name this play by Ariel Dorfman which also titles a Franz Schubert composition.

A gifted young woman receives summer internship as a junior editor at a magazine in New York City in the early 1950s. Eventually Esther Greenwood, who was not totally stable to begin with, goes completely insane. For 10 points-name this novel by Sylvia Plath.

In one song on this album the singer makes a series of gagging noises to suggest Montgomery Clift overdosing. Producer Paul Stevens allegedly overturned chairs during this album's production to create a rock 'n' roll atmosphere. Another song on this album states, "I wasn't born so much as I fell out" and "I came here for a special offer, guaranteed personality". That song is "Lost in the Supermarket". This album's iconic cover is an image of bassist Paul Simonon smashing his guitar. One song on this album claims "you didn't stand by me" while another states "the ice age is coming, the sun is moving in". For 10 points, name this 1979 double album by The Clash, with a title track about radio broadcasts from an English city.

The last of them begins "YES, I have deceived you; I have led away your eunuchs; I have made sport of your jealousy," and is written by Roxana. The 14th includes a discussion of the Troglodites, and the 81st famously includes the author's theories on government. Several were written in Tauris and the Seraglio at Ispahan. The 93rd discusses the death of Louis XIV, and is written by Usbek, one of the two main authors along with Rica. Published anonymously in 1721, FTP, name this series of 161 fictitious epistles, purported to be written by various Arabs, but actually written by Montesquieu.

The town of Moshi lies on the south slopes of this mountain, which Douglas Adams climbed in a rhino suit for charity. The highest of this mountain's three cones, Kibo Peak, is a dormant volcano that has lost a significant portion of its ice cap in recent years. It is located roughly 300 miles southeast of Lake Victoria on the border between Kenya and Tanzania. For 10 points, name this tallest mountain in Africa.

He abandons his short-lived plans to flee to Sweden in his first published book, the memoir If I Die in a Combat Zone, Box Me Up and Ship Me Home. The title character's trek to Paris is revealed to be the imaginings of Paul Berlin in this author's novel Going After Cacciato. This author's most famous work is a collection of short stories, the last of which tells the story of his childhood love, Linda, who died of brain cancer. In another of those stories, "Speaking of Courage," Norman Bowker drives around the lake in his hometown thinking of Kiowa's death. The collection is titled after its first story, which is told primarily from the point of view of First Lieutenant Jimmy Cross, who obsesses over a girl back home named Martha. It also includes extensive lists including items ranging from comic books and M&M's to M-79 grenade launchers. For 10 points, name this American Vietnam War veteran and author of The Things They Carried.

This character tells Theseus that "only the gods can never age" in a play in which he seeks refuge in Colonus. This man was given his name, meaning "swollen feet," by a shepherd at three days of age. His sons Eteocles and Polyneices kill each other in a duel. This character partially fulfilled a prophecy by killing a drunken chariot driver. This husband of Jocasta blinds himself when he discovers that his four children are also his grandchildren. For 10 points, name this Greek antihero who killed his father and married his mother in a Sophocles trilogy.

This author earned a place in Ezra Pound's Imagist Anthology following the publication of his poetry collection Chamber Music. A collection of short stories by this man includes one about a gathering of politicians, "Ivy Day in the Committee Room," as well as one in which a party hosted by the Morkan sisters is attended by Gabriel Conroy. This author of "The Dead" wrote a novel about the coming of age of Stephen Dedalus, a character who also appears in a novel by this man in which Blazes Boylan carries on an affair with Molly, the wife of Leopold Bloom. For 10 points, name this Irish author of Dubliners, A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man and Ulysses.

this structure is essential for complement system. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this phagocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The phagocyte is a key component of the Immune system, involved in complement system.

parts.text: Identify this group, consisting mainly of World War I veterans and their families, that marched on and camped in Washington D.C. in 1932 hoping that they would receive their namesake compensation.
The Bonus Army marched into Washington D.C. during the tenure of this president, who eventually ordered the U.S. Army to dispel the protestors.
The U.S. Army Regiment that dispelled the protestors was led by this noted general, who later oversaw the occupation of Japan.

bonuses.leadin: It was led by Walter Waters and sought payment promised by the Adjusted Service Certificate Law of 1924. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 1892 labor action which ended in violence at the namesake plant outside Pittsburgh.
This Carnegie Company chairman and art benefactor took a hard line against the strikers, leading to his nonfatal shooting and stabbing by anarchist Alexander Berkman.

Alexander Berkman was dispatched to kill Frick by this female companion, who expounded her anarchist views in the journal Mother Earth, the book The Social Significance of the Modern Drama, and the anti-Bolshevik chronicle My Disillusionment in Russia.

bonuses.leadin: It pitted the Amalgamated Association of Iron, Steel, and Tin Workers against Pinkerton detectives at a Carnegie Steel plant. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this Italian-language term for gritty crime films from the 1960s and 70s such as Investigation of a Citizen Above Suspicion. Fernando Di Leo's films from this subgenre like Caliber 9 comment on the Years of Lead.

A Di Leo poliziotteschi film is titled in English for the "Italian" one of these things. A chase scene involving an elevated train appears in a 1971 William Friedkin thriller titled for a "French" one of these things.

William Friedkin's other transit-related thrillers included Sorcerer, a loose remake of this 1953 Henri-Georges Clouzot film, in which two men attempt to drive a truckload of nitroglycerin through the South American wilderness.

bonuses.leadin: In a film in this subgenre, a junkyard kitten gets caught in a firefight that concludes when a framed pimp uses a crane to crush an American hitman. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Greek philosopher who argued that pleasure was the greatest good.
The Epicureans superseded an earlier group of hedonist philosophers led by Aristippus, who were based in this namesake African city.
The Epicurean philosopher Lucretius argued that if humans have free will, atoms could not always fall, but must also have this unpredictable characteristic.

bonuses.leadin: This philosopher argued that a good life is characterized by both the absence of pain, or aponia, and tranquillity, or ataraxia. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel in which the unnamed narrator meets Jack and joins the Brotherhood. It ends with a riot led by Ras the Exhorter.
Invisible Man is a work of this author who also wrote Shadow and Act.
In Invisible Man, the narrator works under Mr. Kimbro at one of these locations, whose products are supposedly the purest white that can be found.

bonuses.leadin: It opens with the narrator blindfolded with several other people in a "battle royal." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This largest freshwater lake by volume can be found in Russia. It is also the world's deepest, at over a mile deep.
This largest Antarctic lake is named for a nearby Russian science station.
Lake Vostok is covered by ice, making it this type of lake first hypothesized about by Russian anarchist philosopher Peter Kropotkin.

bonuses.leadin: For ten points each, answer some questions about deep lakes:

parts.text: Identify this bird instructed to sing in a song that opens with the line, "Sumer is icumen in."
One four-line Middle English lyric addresses this entity prior to the speaker wishing he were in his bed again. This entity is called the "breath of Autumn's being" in an ode by Shelley.
In another short Middle English lyric, the speaker begins, "I am of" this place, and ends by asking the listener to "come and dance with me" in this place.

bonuses.leadin: This bird is addressed in a lyric which states, "Ewe bleteth after lamb, loweth after calve cow, bulloc sterteth, bucke verteth." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this surname of the Ojibwe ("oh-JEEB-way") author Louise, whose 2020 novel The Night Watchman draws on the history of a factory in the Turtle Mountain Indian Reservation. Her sister with this surname, Heid ("hide"), is a poet who wrote the cookbook Original Local.
In "The Theft Outright," Heid E. Erdrich writes, "We were the land's before we were," inverting the opening line of this poet's "The Gift Outright." He also wrote "Mending Wall."

In The Night Watchman, Thomas Wazhashk ("wah-ZHUSHK") leaves at his station a cryptic message about an ominous one of these animals. In Rudolfo Anaya's Bless Me, Ultima, the title character dies after Tenorio kills one of these animals representing her soul.

bonuses.leadin: A novel by an author with this surname features Pixie Parenteau ("PAY-ren-toh"), who is made to swim in a costume of Babe the Blue Ox while working at a nightclub. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these usually concrete, paved areas raised above the sides of roads.

Sidewalks are often paired with these protected areas without barriers to traffic located on the shoulders of roads. They usually "flow" in the direction of traffic and are distinct from cycle tracks.

Bike lanes and sidewalks are at the sides of roads, but lanes dedicated to these systems are at the centers of bidirectional roads. They often have off-board payments and are level with their stations.

bonuses.leadin: In Vancouver, these areas decrease in completeness and in number with distance from the center of the city. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with types of joints.
What is the main function of the synovial in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to types of joints.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Identify this area of the genome, found on chromosome 6 in humans, which controls the structure of the human leukocyte antigen molecules.
Antigens displayed by the class II MHC bind to receptors on the 'helper' variety of these lymphocytes, which also come in a cytotoxic, or 'killer' form.
Class I MHC proteins, on the other hand, bind to this co-receptor for the TCR. It exists as a dimer and can also present itself in natural killer cells.

bonuses.leadin: The proteins encoded by it control immune response by recognition of both self and non-self antigens. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this city where the refugee Sepha Stephanos bonds with Naomi over The Brothers Karamazov in The Beautiful Things That Heaven Bears. A cemetery in this city inspired George Saunders's novel Lincoln in the Bardo.

The former Korean ambassador George Jum extols D.C.'s "beautiful girls" in this 1937 novel about Chungpa Han's adventures among East Coast expats. This Younghill Kang novel was republished in Penguin's Asian American Masterpieces series.
acceptableAnswers: East Goes West: The Making of an Oriental Yankee

parts.text: Alexander Chee's introduction to East Goes West argues that the novel is "erased" by labeling it as this genre. An essay collection by Chee is titled "how to write" this kind of novel, one example of which is Maya Angelou's I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings.
acceptableAnswers: How to Write an Autobiographical Novel

bonuses.leadin: This city is the primary setting of Edward P. Jones's collections Lost in the City and All Aunt Hagar's Children. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The anonymously written book The Mongrel Pillow, which contains such sections as "Things That Stand One's Hair on End," is a parody of this Heian-period author's observations of courtly life.

The disaffected Zen acolyte Mizoguchi becomes distracted by a stray dog in The Temple of the Golden Pavilion, a novel by this author, before eventually burning down the title building at the end of the novel.
The lines "The dog was trampled upon by a cat in heat" is a translation of one of the haiku by this master of the genre, who also wrote the travelogue The Narrow Road to the Deep North.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about dogs in Japanese literature.

parts.text: Name this painting whose foreground and background figures all wear black, in contrast to the white coats of a later painting of a similar subject by the same artist named for David Hayes Agnew.
This Philadelphia-based artist depicted himself studiously taking notes in The Gross Clinic.

In the Philadelphia Museum of Art, The Gross Clinic hangs next to a painting of The Annunciation modeled on a young Palestinian girl by this artist, a student of Eakins. This artist painted a prayer before a meal in The Thankful Poor.

bonuses.leadin: This painting includes a partial self-portrait of the artist on the far right side, in which he is writing intently while looking over a railing towards the central scene. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this work which attempts to reformulate Aristotelian moral thought for modern applications while abandoning its untenable "metaphysical biology."
After Virtue is the most famous work of this Thomist philosopher, whose other books include Dependent Rational Animals and Three Rival Versions of Moral Enquiry.

In After Virtue, MacIntyre glibly dismisses as unproblematic for his position this distinction, first formulated by Hume, which suggests that moral facts cannot be derived from physical ones. According to MacIntyre, a sea captain should just do whatever it is that sea captains do and that's that.

bonuses.leadin: The arguments of this book were expanded in its author's later Whose Justice? Which Rationality? For 10 points each:

parts.text: Ontario shares borders with the Great Lakes and five U.S. states. Name any two of those states.
The majority of Superman II ["two"] was filmed at the Table Rock Welcome Centre near this famous landmark, a natural feature that spans the border between Ontario and New York.
This large body of saltwater, located directly north of Ontario, was named for the Englishman who explored it on his ship Discovery .

bonuses.leadin: For ten points each, answer these questions about Canada's most populated province, Ontario:

parts.text: This form of lyrical, couplet-based love poem exists in both Arabic and Persian literature, and was the form used by the tremendously popular Shirazian poet Hafez. Jamil and Umar were some of its Arabic practitioners.
Reminiscent of The Arabian Nights is this author's Masnavi, or Spiritual Couplets. This student of Shams also wrote Seven Sermons and Fihi ma Fihi.

At the heart of this poetic work by 'Attār is a "clever" pun - the thirty remaining members of the title group discover that they are Simurgh, the wise creature who they traveled seven valleys to find.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Sufi literature, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this children's book author and illustrator whose books In the Night Kitchen and Outside Over There are part of a trilogy with his most famous work.
That most famous work by Sendak is this book about Max's trip through a jungle after being sent to bed without supper.
acceptableAnswers: The Where the Wild Things Are

parts.text: Sendak is also known for illustrating a children's book series by Else Minarik about this title character, his mother and his animal friends.

bonuses.leadin: This author's first book, Kenny's Window, was also illustrated by him. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this existentialist novel about the apathetic Meursault [mer-SO], who shoots an Arab man on the beach.

The Stranger begins by Meursault noting the death of this relative of his that day. His placing of her in a nursing home and his lack of tears at her funeral is used as evidence against him at his trial.

The Stranger is by this French-Algerian author, who wrote of a quarantine of the city of Oran in The Plague and about living in spite of the futility of life in the philosophical treatise The Myth of Sisyphus .

bonuses.leadin: This novel's protagonist has a fairly empty relationship with Marie, and his neighbor, Salamano, suffers from a skin condition.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with liver functions.
What is the main function of the liver in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to liver functions.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.
